# TypeShade

TypeShade is a shader language built around the TypeScript authoring experience. A TypeShade source file starts with `"use typeshade"` and uses TypeScript-shaped syntax to describe GPU programs.

## Start here

- [Introduction](/guide/introduction/): understand the TypeScript-to-TypeShade model.
- [Quick start](/guide/quick-start/): write your first TypeShade shader.
- [Language guide](/guide/language/): learn the language surface.
- [Types](/guide/language/types/): TypeScript types and TypeShade GPU value layout.
- [Functions](/guide/language/functions/): functions, parameters, returns, and shader entry points.
- [Control flow](/guide/language/control-flow/): expressions and supported control flow.
- [GPU types](/guide/language/gpu-types/): scalars, vectors, matrices, and arrays.
- [Resources](/guide/language/resources/): uniforms, storage resources, and declarations.
- [Shader stages](/guide/language/stages/): compute, vertex, and fragment entry points.
- [Examples](/guide/examples/): complete examples and generated shader output.

## Authoring model

TypeShade keeps the TypeScript-shaped authoring model while adding shader-specific semantics. The language boundary is explicit:

```ts
"use typeshade"
```

Shader inputs are explicit function parameters. Builtins are not injected as implicit globals:

```ts
@compute([64, 1, 1])
export function paint(
  @builtin("global_invocation_id") gid: vec3u
) {
  const i = gid.x
  pixels[i] = pixels[i] + camera.pos.x
}
```

GPU resources are declared explicitly:

```ts
declare const camera: uniform<Camera>
declare let pixels: storage<array<f32>>
```

## TypeScript context

When learning TypeShade, the following TypeScript concepts are useful background:

- types and type aliases
- functions and parameters
- classes and fields
- modules and exports
- expressions and control flow

TypeShade documentation explains where these concepts remain familiar and where GPU-specific rules apply.

## Compiler and internals

- [Compiler internals](/guide/internals/): compiler architecture and the internal authoring reference.
- [TypeShade surface specification](https://github.com/typeshade/typeshade/blob/main/docs/use-typeshade-surface.md): source-level language surface and lowering model.
- [TypeShade compiler](https://github.com/typeshade/typeshade): implementation and tests.

## Generated targets

TypeShade lowers its language representation to host-consumable shader source, including WGSL and GLSL ES 3.00. TypeShade does not require a runtime library in the generated shader itself; the host application consumes the generated shader source.

## Documentation principle

Prefer the user-facing language guide before reading compiler internals. The intended learning path is:

TypeScript concepts → `"use typeshade"` → TypeShade language → GPU concepts → examples → compiler internals.
